### In-Memory Transport Example

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/clients/transports.mdx

Demonstrates connecting to a FastMCP server instance within the same Python process using in-memory transport.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP, Client
import os

mcp = FastMCP("TestServer")

@mcp.tool
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    prefix = os.environ.get("GREETING_PREFIX", "Hello")
    return f"{prefix}, {name}!"

client = Client(mcp)

async with client:
    result = await client.call_tool("greet", {"name": "World"})
```

### Test FastMCP Tools Using In-Memory Transport (Python)

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/development/tests.mdx

Test FastMCP server functionality directly by passing the server instance to the client, enabling deterministic and fast execution within the same Python process without network overhead.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP, Client

# Create your server
server = FastMCP("WeatherServer")

@server.tool
def get_temperature(city: str) -> dict:
    """Get current temperature for a city"""
    temps = {"NYC": 72, "LA": 85, "Chicago": 68}
    return {"city": city, "temp": temps.get(city, 70)}

async def test_weather_operations():
    # Pass server directly - no deployment needed
    async with Client(server) as client:
        result = await client.call_tool("get_temperature", {"city": "NYC"})
        assert result.data == {"city": "NYC", "temp": 72}
```

### Adding Middleware to a Proxy Server

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/server.py

Shows how to add custom middleware to a proxy using add_middleware().

```python
from fastmcp.server import create_proxy
from fastmcp.server.middleware import Middleware, MiddlewareContext, CallNext
from fastmcp import FastMCP

class MetricsMiddleware(Middleware):
    async def on_call_tool(self, context: MiddlewareContext, call_next: CallNext):
        tool_name = context.params.name
        return await call_next(context)

original_server = FastMCP("MyServer")
proxy = create_proxy(original_server)
proxy.add_middleware(MetricsMiddleware())
```

### Adding Proxied Components to Existing Server

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/servers/providers/proxy.mdx

Demonstrates how to mount proxied tools from an external FastMCP server onto an existing local FastMCP server, combining local and proxied functionalities.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.server import create_proxy

server = FastMCP("My Server")

# Add local tools
@server.tool
def local_tool() -> str:
    return "Local result"

# Mount proxied tools from another server
external = create_proxy("http://external-server/mcp")
server.mount(external)

# Now server has both local and proxied tools
```

### ProxyProvider: client_factory and cache_ttl semantics

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/providers/proxy.py

ProxyProvider.__init__ accepts a client_factory callable (sync or async) that is invoked per-request to create Client instances. Component lists are cached with a default 300s TTL; cache_ttl=0 disables caching entirely. The cache is lazily refreshed on list_* calls and entries expire when time.monotonic() - timestamp >= ttl.
